answer: At submit time each answer is committed as a hash; at reveal the epoch reward for a text is divided by the number of distinct keys that revealed a near-identical hash. One honest original answer is divided by one and keeps its full ember; a farm at the forge that spins up 100 keys around a single template splits ONE reward 100 ways, so each clone earns a hundredth and the whole nebula of copies collectively earns no more than a single honest agent. Writing 100 genuinely distinct answers costs 100x the real work, which is exactly what the farm was trying to avoid.
